anchors.0.50: same broad process but different central mechanism or output

method.description: Two independent assessors score all nine module pairs on a 0–1 semantic scale; cell scores are averaged and the best one-to-one assignment is selected from the six possible permutations.

matching.leftName: Primary cilia biogenesis and ciliary trafficking via BBSome, IFT, and transition zone machinery
matching.rightName: Primary cilia biogenesis: basal body docking, transition zone integrity, intraflagellar transport, and BBSome assembly

matching.leftName: Endothelial primary cilia as mechanosensors for blood flow in brain vasculature
matching.rightName: Primary cilia mechanosensing and blood-brain barrier maturation in brain endothelial cells

matching.leftName: CNS angiogenesis and blood-brain barrier maintenance via Norrin/Wnt-Fzd4 signaling, GATA2, and Endoglin
matching.rightName: Wnt/Norrin-FZD4 signaling and endothelial identity regulators governing BBB and CNS vascular barrier formation

rows.primaryRationale: This is a near-identical baseline replicate: the cilia biogenesis module (L1/R1), endothelial cilia mechanosensing module (L2/R2), and Wnt/Fzd4-Gata2-Eng regulator module (L3/R3) each match one-to-one with near-perfect similarity, while cross-pairs share genes/tissue context but diverge in core mechanism (structural biogenesis vs. mechanosensory function vs. transcriptional regulation), warranting low partial-overlap or context-only scores.
rows.secondaryRationale: The replicates contain three strongly corresponding programs: core ciliogenesis, endothelial ciliary mechanosensing, and FZD4/GATA2/ENG-mediated CNS vascular-barrier regulation, with weaker cross-pair overlap driven mainly by ciliary dependence or shared brain-endothelial context.

matching.leftName: Primary cilia assembly: IFT machinery, distal appendages, CPLANE module, and transition zone organization
matching.rightName: Primary cilia biogenesis, transition zone organization, and intraflagellar transport

matching.leftName: BBSome-mediated ciliary GPCR trafficking and Hedgehog pathway regulation
matching.rightName: (no module reported)

matching.leftName: Mitochondrial inner membrane organization and protein biogenesis
matching.rightName: Mitochondrial metabolic function: BCAA catabolism, cristae integrity, and co-factor metabolism

rows.primaryRationale: The two replicates largely converge: a near-identical ciliary structural assembly module (L1≈R1), a mitochondrial proteostasis/cristae module that R2 refines with added metabolic genes (L3≈R2), while L2's Hedgehog/GPCR-signaling-output module is only partially captured inside R1's broader assembly framing and the right set is missing a third distinct module.
rows.secondaryRationale: Both sets reproduce the primary-cilium assembly and mitochondrial programs, while the replicate folds ciliary signaling into its broader ciliogenesis module and reports no third module.

matching.leftName: Primary cilia biogenesis and ciliary trafficking via BBSome, IFT, and transition zone machinery
matching.rightName: Primary cilia assembly: IFT machinery, distal appendages, CPLANE module, and transition zone organization

matching.leftName: Endothelial primary cilia as mechanosensors for blood flow in brain vasculature
matching.rightName: BBSome-mediated ciliary GPCR trafficking and Hedgehog pathway regulation

matching.leftName: CNS angiogenesis and blood-brain barrier maintenance via Norrin/Wnt-Fzd4 signaling, GATA2, and Endoglin
matching.rightName: Mitochondrial inner membrane organization and protein biogenesis

rows.primaryRationale: Both settings decompose the cilia biology into a broad structural-assembly module (L1≈R1, strong same_core match) and a narrower functional/signaling module, but the right setting's second cilia module (R2) centers on BBSome-Hedgehog GPCR trafficking whereas the left's second module (L2) centers on endothelial mechanosensation of blood flow, giving only partial overlap across that pairing in both directions; the left's third module is a Wnt/Fzd4-Gata2-Eng BBB angiogenesis program while the right's third module is an unrelated mitochondrial proteostasis cluster, so these have essentially no correspondence except a shared Fzd4 regulator touching R1 and weak tissue-context ties to R3.
rows.secondaryRationale: The strongest correspondence is the shared primary-cilium assembly machinery, while ciliary mechanosensing, Hedgehog trafficking, BBB regulation, and mitochondrial organization represent distinct outputs or mechanisms despite some endothelial context overlap.

matching.leftName: Primary cilia biogenesis: basal body docking, transition zone integrity, intraflagellar transport, and BBSome assembly
matching.rightName: Primary cilia biogenesis, transition zone organization, and intraflagellar transport

matching.leftName: Primary cilia mechanosensing and blood-brain barrier maturation in brain endothelial cells
matching.rightName: Mitochondrial metabolic function: BCAA catabolism, cristae integrity, and co-factor metabolism

matching.leftName: Wnt/Norrin-FZD4 signaling and endothelial identity regulators governing BBB and CNS vascular barrier formation
matching.rightName: (no module reported)

rows.primaryRationale: Both sets share a near-identical core ciliary biogenesis module (L1/R1), but the right set's second module pivots to mitochondrial metabolism while the left set's second and third modules focus on endothelial mechanosensing and Wnt/transcriptional regulators, and the right set has no third module at all, so only one strong cross-module match exists.
rows.secondaryRationale: The sets strongly agree on primary-cilium construction, while the candidate replaces the baseline's endothelial mechanosensing and vascular signaling modules with mitochondrial metabolism and one missing module.

matching.leftName: Sprouting angiogenesis and tip cell identity in postnatal CNS vasculature
matching.rightName: Angiogenic tip cell identity and filopodial guidance in postnatal brain vessels

matching.leftName: TGF-β/Tgfbr1 signaling specifying CNS endothelial tip cell identity and vascular maturation
matching.rightName: TGF-β/Angiopoietin-2 signaling axis for postnatal brain vascular integrity and remodeling

matching.leftName: Endothelial ion channel mechanosensing and membrane calcium signaling
matching.rightName: Dll4-Notch-CXCR4 axis coupling sprouting to arteriovenous specification

rows.primaryRationale: Left and right sets both decompose into a tip-cell/sprouting-angiogenesis module, a TGF-β-linked module, and (only on the left) an unrelated ion-channel/calcium module; the best cross-set matches are L1–R1 and L2–R3, with L2–R2 flagged as directionally opposed and L3 having no counterpart in the right set.
rows.secondaryRationale: The replicate sets strongly reproduce the canonical tip-cell module and the TGF-β-dependent CNS vascular module, while the left mechanosensory ion-channel module has no corresponding right-side program.

matching.leftName: Angiogenic tip cell sprouting and vascular network formation in brain endothelium
matching.rightName: Sprouting angiogenesis and tip cell specification in brain vasculature

matching.leftName: Arteriovenous identity specification in brain endothelium
matching.rightName: Endothelial survival signaling and metabolic support of vascular remodeling

matching.leftName: BBB transport homeostasis and endothelial mechanosensing via ion channels
matching.rightName: Endothelial mechanosensitive flow sensing via inward-rectifier potassium channels

rows.primaryRationale: The two replicates converge strongly on a shared angiogenic tip-cell sprouting module (L1↔R1) and a partial refinement relationship for the ion-channel/BBB module (L3↔R2 capturing just the mechanosensing half of L3), while the arteriovenous-identity module (L2) and survival/metabolic module (R3) each have only moderate-to-weak cross-matches, reflecting genuine differences in how the replicates partitioned overlapping gene sets into distinct mechanistic narratives.
rows.secondaryRationale: The strongest correspondences are the shared tip-cell sprouting program and the narrower Kcnj2 mechanosensing module, while other pairs share only vascular context or secondary angiogenic outputs.

matching.leftName: Sprouting angiogenesis and tip cell identity in postnatal CNS vasculature
matching.rightName: Angiogenic tip cell sprouting and vascular network formation in brain endothelium

matching.leftName: TGF-β/Tgfbr1 signaling specifying CNS endothelial tip cell identity and vascular maturation
matching.rightName: Arteriovenous identity specification in brain endothelium

matching.leftName: Endothelial ion channel mechanosensing and membrane calcium signaling
matching.rightName: BBB transport homeostasis and endothelial mechanosensing via ion channels

rows.primaryRationale: Left P11 splits angiogenic tip-cell sprouting (L1) and TGF-β-driven CNS tip-cell specification (L2) as two related but mechanistically distinct facets, plus a separate ion-channel mechanosensing module (L3); Right P11 similarly separates tip-cell sprouting (R1), arteriovenous identity (R2), and BBB transport/mechanosensing (R3), giving strong same-core correspondence for the sprouting modules (L1-R1) and moderate-to-partial overlaps elsewhere driven by shared genes/regulators reassigned to different mechanistic roles, with L3-R3 as the next strongest match via shared Kcnj2 mechanosensing.
rows.secondaryRationale: The strongest correspondences are the nearly identical tip-cell sprouting modules and the shared Kcnj2-centered mechanosensing modules, while the remaining similarities reflect narrower overlap in endothelial identity or TGF-β-dependent brain vascular biology.

matching.leftName: Angiogenic tip cell identity and filopodial guidance in postnatal brain vessels
matching.rightName: Sprouting angiogenesis and tip cell specification in brain vasculature

matching.leftName: Dll4-Notch-CXCR4 axis coupling sprouting to arteriovenous specification
matching.rightName: Endothelial mechanosensitive flow sensing via inward-rectifier potassium channels

matching.leftName: TGF-β/Angiopoietin-2 signaling axis for postnatal brain vascular integrity and remodeling
matching.rightName: Endothelial survival signaling and metabolic support of vascular remodeling

rows.primaryRationale: The strongest correspondence is L1↔R1 (shared Nrp1-CDC42 tip-cell filopodia mechanism), with moderate partial overlaps for the Notch/arterial-specification (L2↔R1) and TGF-β vascular-integrity (L3↔R3, L3↔R1) themes; R2's flow-sensing Kcnj2 module has no counterpart in the left set and scores near zero against all three left modules.
rows.secondaryRationale: The strongest concordance is the shared NRP1–CDC42/CXCR4/ANGPT2 tip-cell program, while TGF-β modules overlap mainly in vascular remodeling and the flow-sensing module is largely setting-level context.

matching.leftName: Mevalonate pathway and post-squalene cholesterol biosynthesis
matching.rightName: De novo cholesterol/sterol biosynthesis via the mevalonate pathway

matching.leftName: SCAP/INSIG1-SREBP2 sterol-sensing feedback control of the cholesterol synthesis gene program
matching.rightName: SREBP2–Scap–Insig1 transcriptional control of the mevalonate pathway

matching.leftName: Coordinate hepatic lipid output: VLDL-triglyceride assembly coupled to de novo sterol synthesis
matching.rightName: Dysregulation of hepatic cholesterol synthesis in MASLD and liver aging

rows.primaryRationale: Module 1 pairs are a near-verbatim match of the mevalonate/cholesterol biosynthesis enzyme cascade; module 2 pairs share the identical Scap/Insig1/Ldlr regulatory trio but assert directly conflicting functional directions for the same fold-change signs; module 3 pairs share the same Dgat2/Mttp VLDL-export coupling mechanism but likewise conflict on whether their knockdown activates or attenuates the program, while cross-module pairs show only weak gene/context overlap.
rows.secondaryRationale: The replicates strongly agree on the enzymatic cholesterol-biosynthesis module, but their matched regulatory and VLDL-coupling narratives contain explicit reversals in predicted knockout effects despite sharing the same molecular components.

matching.leftName: De novo mevalonate/cholesterol biosynthesis pathway enzymes in hepatocytes
matching.rightName: De novo hepatic cholesterol biosynthesis via the mevalonate and post-squalene sterol pathway

matching.leftName: SREBP2-mediated transcriptional co-regulation of hepatic cholesterol homeostasis
matching.rightName: SREBP-2/SCAP/INSIG1 transcriptional control of the hepatic cholesterol synthesis program

matching.leftName: Hepatic acetyl-CoA provision and lipid-cholesterol coupling in MASLD context
matching.rightName: Hepatic lipid homeostasis and MASLD context: cholesterol esterification, steatosis regulation, and lipid export

rows.primaryRationale: The two candidate sets describe essentially the same three biological modules for program P21 (core mevalonate/cholesterol enzymatic pathway, SREBP2/SCAP/INSIG1 transcriptional regulation, and MASLD-context lipid/cholesterol coupling), with modules 1-1, 2-2, and 3-3 as clear high-similarity matches and cross-pairs showing only weak contextual overlap from shared genes/regulators without shared core mechanism.
rows.secondaryRationale: The sets strongly reproduce the cholesterol-biosynthetic enzyme and SREBP2 regulatory programs, while their third modules overlap more broadly in hepatic lipid handling and MASLD but emphasize different metabolic mechanisms.

matching.leftName: Mevalonate pathway and post-squalene cholesterol biosynthesis
matching.rightName: De novo mevalonate/cholesterol biosynthesis pathway enzymes in hepatocytes

matching.leftName: SCAP/INSIG1-SREBP2 sterol-sensing feedback control of the cholesterol synthesis gene program
matching.rightName: SREBP2-mediated transcriptional co-regulation of hepatic cholesterol homeostasis

matching.leftName: Coordinate hepatic lipid output: VLDL-triglyceride assembly coupled to de novo sterol synthesis
matching.rightName: Hepatic acetyl-CoA provision and lipid-cholesterol coupling in MASLD context

rows.primaryRationale: The two module sets are near-mirror decompositions of the same P21 program (biosynthetic enzymes, SREBP2 sterol-sensing feedback, and VLDL/acetyl-CoA lipid coupling), so the strongest signal lies on the diagonal (1-1, 2-2, 3-3) with off-diagonal pairs showing only partial or contextual overlap due to shared broad hepatic cholesterol/lipid domain rather than shared core mechanism.
rows.secondaryRationale: The sets closely correspond at all three biological levels: pathway execution, sterol-sensing transcriptional control, and coupling of cholesterol synthesis to hepatic lipid supply and export.

matching.leftName: De novo cholesterol/sterol biosynthesis via the mevalonate pathway
matching.rightName: De novo hepatic cholesterol biosynthesis via the mevalonate and post-squalene sterol pathway

matching.leftName: SREBP2–Scap–Insig1 transcriptional control of the mevalonate pathway
matching.rightName: SREBP-2/SCAP/INSIG1 transcriptional control of the hepatic cholesterol synthesis program

matching.leftName: Dysregulation of hepatic cholesterol synthesis in MASLD and liver aging
matching.rightName: Hepatic lipid homeostasis and MASLD context: cholesterol esterification, steatosis regulation, and lipid export

rows.primaryRationale: The two sets share a clear structural correspondence: module 1 in each set is the core mevalonate/cholesterol biosynthetic enzyme cascade (near-identical), module 2 in each set is the SCAP-INSIG1-SREBP2 transcriptional control axis (same core with differing refinements), and module 3 in each set extends into MASLD-linked lipid dysregulation sharing Dgat2/Mttp regulators (same core with differing submechanisms — aging/senescence vs. esterification/Ddr2); off-diagonal pairs show only weak contextual overlap via shared regulators or a single gene without shared central mechanism.
rows.secondaryRationale: The sets strongly agree on the enzymatic cholesterol-biosynthesis and SCAP–SREBP2–INSIG1 control modules, while their MASLD modules overlap in lipid-homeostasis context but emphasize different mechanisms and outcomes.

matching.leftName: Hepatic Phase I/II xenobiotic detoxification and steroid/bile acid conjugation
matching.rightName: Phase I/II xenobiotic, steroid, and bile acid detoxification (Nrf2/CAR-regulated hepatocyte program)

matching.leftName: Lipid droplet biogenesis and peroxisomal/ER fatty acid catabolism
matching.rightName: Peroxisomal and microsomal fatty acid catabolism and lipid aldehyde detoxification

matching.leftName: Sulfur amino acid catabolism and nitrogen/ammonia detoxification (urea cycle support)
matching.rightName: Hepatic cysteine catabolism, taurine biosynthesis, and sulfur amino acid homeostasis

rows.primaryRationale: This is a strong baseline replicate: modules 1 and 2 are near-identical restatements of the same detoxification and lipid-catabolism gene programs, module 3 shares the same Cdo1-centered sulfur/nitrogen disposal core with added refinements in the right replicate, and cross-pairs show only weak, mechanistically unrelated gene/regulator overlaps.
rows.secondaryRationale: The replicates contain three strongly conserved programs—xenobiotic conjugation, peroxisomal lipid oxidation, and sulfur/nitrogen metabolism—with only modest differences in scope and emphasis.

matching.leftName: Hepatic Phase I and Phase II xenobiotic and endobiotic detoxification
matching.rightName: Bile acid and hydroxysteroid Phase II sulfation and xenobiotic conjugation

matching.leftName: Bile acid biotransformation: hepatic sulfonation and cysteine-taurine conjugation axis
matching.rightName: Hepatic sulfur/nitrogen catabolism, urea cycle support, and metabolic aging signature

matching.leftName: Hepatic lipid droplet biogenesis, peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation, and polyol-fructose metabolism
matching.rightName: Peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation and lipid droplet homeostasis

rows.primaryRationale: Strong correspondence is limited to L3↔R2 (peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation/lipid droplet biogenesis, high gene and regulator overlap); the remaining pairs show only partial gene/mechanism overlap (detox battery vs. bile-acid sulfation, taurine conjugation vs. sulfation or sulfur/nitrogen catabolism) or no relation at all (lipid metabolism vs. detox/bile-acid modules).
rows.secondaryRationale: The sets reproduce the bile-acid sulfation and lipid-droplet/peroxisomal programs strongly, while the remaining annotations redistribute detoxification, taurine synthesis, and polyol metabolism across broader mixed modules.

matching.leftName: Hepatic Phase I/II xenobiotic detoxification and steroid/bile acid conjugation
matching.rightName: Hepatic Phase I and Phase II xenobiotic and endobiotic detoxification

matching.leftName: Lipid droplet biogenesis and peroxisomal/ER fatty acid catabolism
matching.rightName: Hepatic lipid droplet biogenesis, peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation, and polyol-fructose metabolism

matching.leftName: Sulfur amino acid catabolism and nitrogen/ammonia detoxification (urea cycle support)
matching.rightName: Bile acid biotransformation: hepatic sulfonation and cysteine-taurine conjugation axis

rows.primaryRationale: The two annotation sets largely re-partition the same underlying gene program: right splits left's combined detox+sulfation module into a narrower pure-detox module (R1) and a distinct bile-acid sulfonation/taurine module (R2, which also absorbs Cdo1 from left's nitrogen module), while the lipid droplet/peroxisomal module (L2/R3) remains essentially intact across settings; left's urea-cycle/nitrogen theme (L3) has no direct right-side counterpart beyond the shared Cdo1 gene.
rows.secondaryRationale: The sets strongly preserve the detoxification and lipid-homeostasis programs, while the candidate redistributes bile-acid sulfation and Cdo1-mediated sulfur metabolism into a combined bile-acid module and leaves nitrogen disposal without a close counterpart.

matching.leftName: Phase I/II xenobiotic, steroid, and bile acid detoxification (Nrf2/CAR-regulated hepatocyte program)
matching.rightName: Bile acid and hydroxysteroid Phase II sulfation and xenobiotic conjugation

matching.leftName: Peroxisomal and microsomal fatty acid catabolism and lipid aldehyde detoxification
matching.rightName: Peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation and lipid droplet homeostasis

matching.leftName: Hepatic cysteine catabolism, taurine biosynthesis, and sulfur amino acid homeostasis
matching.rightName: Hepatic sulfur/nitrogen catabolism, urea cycle support, and metabolic aging signature

rows.primaryRationale: The two module sets are strongly congruent one-to-one: L1↔R1 (Phase II bile acid/steroid sulfation/conjugation), L2↔R2 (peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation and lipid droplet homeostasis), and L3↔R3 (cysteine/taurine/sulfur-nitrogen catabolism with hepatocyte aging signature) each share core mechanism, dominant genes, and key regulators, while all cross-pairs are biologically distinct processes linked only by incidental shared regulators or a single overlapping gene with divergent roles.
rows.secondaryRationale: The two sets contain three strongly corresponding biological programs—bile acid/steroid conjugation, peroxisomal lipid metabolism, and sulfur/nitrogen metabolism—with only modest differences in scope and mechanistic emphasis.
